newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine grain quality suffers after rainy summer.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine grain quality suffers after rainy summer.

text.p: Ukraine's farm minister said on Friday that grain quality would suffer this year after a very rainy summer.
"This year, weather conditions have been such that out of 50 harvest days, only 13 to 14 days have given us an opportunity to work," Yuri Karasyk told parliamentary deputies.
Heavy rains throughout most of July have hampered the harvest.

Karasyk, appointed to head what is now known as the ministry for the agro-industrial complex, said Ukraine had only three million hectares still to harvest, out of 12 million sown this year to spring grains.
Southern regions had completed harvesting, and Ukraine had gathered 23 million tonnes of grain.
He did not provide output forecasts. The government sees net grain output at 37-38 million tonnes this year against 25.4 million tonnes last year.
Karasyk also faulted poor-quality machinery, which can leave up to 30 percent of grain in the fields, for problems with bringing in crops.
Grain dryers have been working overtime to try to save crops gathered from soaked fields.
